title: State of Karnataka v. K.D. Kempamma @ Cyanide Mallika
court_or_authority: High Court of Karnataka / Sessions Court Bangalore
legal_citation: Criminal Appeal No. 744/2010 (Karnataka HC); 2012 SCC OnLine Kar 8901
source: High Court of Karnataka & Indian Kanoon (doc/14101928)
evidence: Recovery of potassium cyanide vials and empty medicine containers from handbag upon arrest at Bangalore bus station
Multiple pawn tickets for recovered gold thalis and mangalsutras belonging to deceased female temple devotees
Witness statements from temple lodge managers identifying suspect checking into guest rooms with victims
Forensic chemical viscera detection confirming lethal cyanide dosage
modus_operandi: Targeted wealthy middle-aged women visiting temples who appeared distressed or praying for domestic resolution. Claimed to be an expert in holy rituals (Mandala Pooja). Convinced victims to stay at nearby budget lodges wearing their finest gold jewelry. Instructed them to close eyes and drink consecrated holy water laced with cyanide. Stole all jewelry and money before fleeing.
personality_disorder: Psychopathic personality with predatory deceit, clinical lack of remorse, and opportunistic financial predation.
common_traits: False pretense of performing Mandala ritual prayers
Use of potassium cyanide in holy water or prasadam
Theft of gold ornaments and mangalsutras
Lodge room crimes near sacred pilgrimage centers
summary: Known as India first convicted female serial killer. Convicted of poisoning and robbing at least six women devotees at temple towns across Karnataka between 1999 and 2007. Sentenced to death, later commuted to life imprisonment without remission.
